radiology_report:
Subject: Multiparametric MRI of the prostate
Date: 28 Jan 2025
Institution: Amsterdam UMC (location AMC)
Clinical context: Assessment prompted by an elevated prostate-specific antigen of 11.0 ng/mL alongside a previously confirmed positive biopsy.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 58.95 mL in volume. A discrete, low-signal abnormality occupies the mid-gland left peripheral zone on T2-weighted images, spanning 12 × 9 × 10 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging coupled with apparent diffusion coefficient mapping reveals marked restriction (elevated signal at b1000, depressed ADC values). Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences highlight prompt, localized enhancement. Extracapsular spread, seminal vesicle infiltration, and suspicious nodal enlargement are absent.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left mid peripheral zone.
PSAD 0.187 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8033811

previous_notes.author: Dr. C. Peters (GP)
previous_notes.text: Follow-up occurred on 04 Jun 2024 after laboratory values demonstrated a PSA increase to 7.0 ng/mL, climbing from the 5.2 ng/mL reading documented in June 2023. A transrectal ultrasound examination was conducted, and a subsequent biopsy was organized for later that year. Driven by the ongoing upward PSA trend and the patient's stated preference for vigilant observation, an outpatient urology appointment was secured for a thorough clinical reassessment.
